answer: Each identity registers one timber beam at a summit yard, locks an 80-credit bond, and pays a load-test fee. A falcon inspector applies a standard load, measures deflection, brands the serial, and publishes serial and curve. A branded beam cannot register again; a second filing under one serial burns both bonds. The first test costs 34 credits and the kth costs 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7027 and 1000 fakes pay 3,530,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-beam ring fails because brand and curve are already public. An honest agent pays 34 once and keeps its bond after passing.
